summary: Frontend-only 4th-attempt retest of the Radar sustained-drag interaction-lock bug, after RadarView's pinch/pan/doubleTap gestures were wrapped in a single useMemo (deps: [mapH, applyZoomState, onInteractionStart, onInteractionEnd]) and applyZoomState in useCallback (empty deps), specifically to stop gesture-object recreation from killing in-progress drags mid-touch. RESULT: BUG STILL REPRODUCES, with new precise evidence showing the root cause is NOT (or not only) gesture-object recreation. Quick tap-down/release x5 cycle: 5/5 PASS (lock engages on down, self-releases to scrollable within ~600ms of release, consistent with iteration_98). Zoom tier stepping via +/- buttons and recentre: 4->9->16->9->4 all correct, and reanimated DOM transform updates were confirmed working for button-driven zoom (scale 1 -> 1.565 visible in computed style) - this proves the DOM-inspection test method is valid and reanimated shared-value->DOM sync works in this environment. CRITICAL RETEST (sustained 1.5-2s single-finger drag): ran 3 separate variants (small 2-3px/80ms increments, larger 8px/50ms increments, and native Playwright mouse.move(steps=40) continuous drag) - in ALL THREE, the outer ScrollView's overflowY dropped from 'hidden' to 'auto' at ~450-460ms (matching the watchdog's exact 450ms timeout) WHILE THE MOUSE WAS STILL DOWN AND CONTINUOUSLY MOVING, and never re-locked for the remaining 1.0-1.5s of simulated drag - same premature-unlock symptom as iteration_98, unchanged by this fix. NEW, more precise finding (per the review request's explicit ask to check tx/ty): the world-layer's computed CSS transform (which carries tx/ty/scale from the pan/pinch gesture) stayed frozen at the exact identity matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) for the ENTIRE duration of every drag variant tested - i.e. the map visually never panned at all, not even during the initial ~450ms while the lock was still correctly engaged. This means Pan's onUpdate handler is not firing/updating shared values in response to synthetic/programmatic mouse-down+mousemove sequences in this Playwright/RNGH-web environment at all (not a timing race after the first ping - it appears never to fire), which independently explains why the interaction-lock's continuous re-ping also never happens: onInteractionStart is only ever called once via onTouchesDown, the 450ms watchdog fires unrefreshed, and the underlying pan gesture recognizer itself appears inert to this input method for its whole duration. No console errors/red screens seen.

integration_issues.flow: Radar touch-interaction watchdog lock + Pan gesture onUpdate (RadarView.tsx pan gesture inside the new useMemo, pinged into app/(tabs)/index.tsx onRadarInteractionStart/End)
integration_issues.issue: STILL CRITICAL, same symptom class as iteration_96/97/98 across 4 fix attempts: during a sustained single-finger drag (mouse held down, continuously moving for 1.5-2s), the ScrollView interaction-lock unlocks at exactly ~450ms (the watchdog's own timeout) and never re-engages for the rest of the gesture. NEW evidence this round: the map's own transform (tx/ty via pan.onUpdate) NEVER changes at all during any drag variant tested (confirmed via 3 different synthetic-drag techniques including native Playwright mouse.move(steps=40)), while the SAME transform DID update correctly for the zoom +/- buttons (scale 1->1.565, tier chip 4->9). This strongly suggests Pan.onUpdate is not firing at all in response to programmatic/simulated mouse-move sequences in this specific web-preview/RNGH environment - the useMemo/useCallback gesture-object-identity fix (this iteration's change) addressed a real potential issue but did not fix the observed symptom, because the actual blocker appears to be upstream: the pan recognizer itself is not receiving continued move events in this test harness, so the fix's premise (state re-renders were killing an already-firing onUpdate) may not be the operative failure mode here at all.

action_items: STILL BROKEN after 4th fix attempt: sustained-drag lock premature-release at ~450ms (exact watchdog timeout) with no recovery for the remainder of the gesture - reproduced 3x with different synthetic-drag techniques including Playwright's native mouse.move(steps=40).

NEW, actionable evidence for main agent: the map's pan transform (tx/ty) itself NEVER changes during the drag in this web-preview test environment - confirmed by inspecting the world-layer's computed CSS transform, which stayed at identity matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) throughout every drag attempt, while the SAME transform correctly updated for zoom +/- button taps (scale 1->1.565) in the same session. This means either (a) RNGH's web Pan recognizer genuinely does not respond to Playwright-simulated mouse events past initial touchdown in this environment (a testing-harness/RNGH-web-pointer-events gap, not a React re-render issue), or (b) there is a real regression where Pan.onUpdate never fires post-recognition on web. Given onTouchesDown fires correctly (lock engages at t=0) but onUpdate produces zero visible effect for the gesture's whole duration, and the watchdog lapses at precisely 450ms with no earlier or later variance across 3 test runs, the simplest explanation consistent with all evidence is that onUpdate simply isn't being invoked by this input method here - not a race/timing bug in the memoized re-render fix.

Given this is the 4th attempt and the underlying gesture-recognizer behavior (not just the lock flag) now shows zero pan movement during synthetic drags, per the agent-to-agent note this is exactly the case for a final call: recommend shipping with a clear caveat that RNGH pan/pinch behavior under this specific web-preview test harness cannot be fully validated by Playwright mouse simulation, and that real-device (iOS/Android Expo Go) testing is required to confirm whether onUpdate actually fires continuously during a real physical drag - the useMemo/useCallback fix itself is architecturally correct (verified in code) and should be kept regardless, but further web-preview-only iteration on this specific symptom is unlikely to be conclusive given the transform-freeze evidence.

Regression (all PASS, no issues): quick tap-down/release x5 cycles (lock engages+self-releases correctly every time); zoom +/- and recentre buttons step focus-chip tier 4->9->16->9->4 correctly with real reanimated transform changes; Filters sheet opens correctly. Did not exercise double-tap-to-zoom or full pinch (2-pointer) in this pass since prior iterations already flagged mouse dblclick/pinch as web-emulation artifacts, and the drag-related evidence gathered was the priority ask.
critical_code_review_comments: The useMemo/useCallback gesture-memoization fix in RadarView.tsx (lines 297-420, 275-278) is correctly implemented and stable across re-renders per code review (mapH/applyZoomState/onInteractionStart/onInteractionEnd are all stable references) - this is good defensive engineering and should not be reverted. However, this iteration's test evidence indicates it does not fix the reported symptom because the underlying failure appears to be that Pan.onUpdate itself never fires during simulated drags in this test environment, independent of gesture object identity.

Recommend adding a lightweight JS-side diagnostic (e.g. a temporary runOnJS counter incremented inside pan.onUpdate, logged to console) in a future debug build so the next tester/agent can directly confirm from console output whether onUpdate is invoked at all during a drag on both web-preview and a real device, rather than inferring it indirectly from the DOM transform (which is a strong proxy but not the same as instrumenting the handler itself).

success_rate.frontend: ~85% - all regression items pass (tap cycles 5/5, zoom tier stepping, filters sheet); the one CRITICAL sustained-drag lock/pan issue this iteration specifically targeted is still failing with new, more conclusive evidence

seed_data_creation: None - used existing kauri@intro.demo demo account via 'Explore Demo' (login-demo) on /login
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login: /login -> [data-testid=login-demo] -> [data-testid=tab-radar]. Dismiss ping popups via get_by_text('Dismiss', exact=True) in a retry loop before interacting with the map. Scroll-lock ancestor: document.querySelector('[data-testid="radar-map"]').parentElement.parentElement -> getComputedStyle().overflowY ('hidden' when locked, 'auto' when unlocked). World-layer transform (tx/ty/scale proxy): walk down from radar-map, depth 3, the child whose className includes 'pointerEvents' -> getComputedStyle().transform (identity 'matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)' = no pan/zoom applied). Confirmed this method is valid: zoom+ button changed it to matrix(1.565,...) reliably. For the drag test, tried 3 methods (slow small steps, fast larger steps, native page.mouse.move(steps=40)) - ALL show frozen identity transform for the whole drag and lock-drop at exactly 450ms unrefreshed. If further debugging is wanted, next step should be adding a temporary onUpdate console/runOnJS counter in RadarView.tsx pan gesture to definitively prove whether onUpdate fires 0 times or >0 times during a Playwright-simulated drag, and cross-check against a real device if possible.
rca_of_issue: This iteration's fix (memoizing gesture construction so GestureDetector never tears down recognizers on re-render) is correct and necessary in principle, but test evidence shows it did not change the observed behavior at all versus iteration_98: the lock still drops at exactly 450ms (the watchdog's own unrefreshed timeout) and the map's transform never changes for the whole gesture in 3 separate synthetic-drag test methods, including Playwright's native multi-step mouse.move. Because the SAME transform inspection technique correctly detected real changes when zoom buttons were pressed (scale 1->1.565) in the same test session, the transform-freeze during drags is not a test-instrumentation artifact - it indicates Pan.onUpdate (and therefore its runOnJS(onInteractionStart) re-ping) is not being invoked at all during these simulated drags in this specific web-preview/RNGH environment, which would fully explain both why the watchdog never gets refreshed and why the map never visibly pans. This points away from the gesture-object-identity theory (this iteration's fix target) and toward either a fundamental gap in how RNGH's web Pan recognizer processes Playwright-simulated pointer/mouse sequences (most likely, given the exact 450ms-unrefreshed timing is identical to a scenario where onUpdate simply never runs), or a genuine, more severe underlying regression where Pan.onUpdate does not fire post-recognition on web at all - either way, this cannot be conclusively distinguished without either device testing or an instrumented debug build, matching the original agent-to-agent request for a final call.
